g.text: Training map: an invented farming area (original, not a real place)
At 1:50,000, 1 cm on the map = 500 m on the ground only when this
image is printed 20 cm wide (grid squares 2 cm). At any other
size, measure with the scale bar.
Title: the area and purpose, an invented training area, so no
real-place facts can be read from it.
Key: what each symbol and colour means, e.g. contours (10 m
interval), roads, river, cultivation, school and clinic.
Scale 1:50,000 and bar: ground distances (1 cm = 500 m at print
size). Grid-north arrow: direction and bearings.
None of these shows how reliable a service is, its opening hours
The key identifies a school at D (education) and a clinic at C
Roads join A to D and D to C, so the map shows a connection
Cultivated fields are keyed separately, north-west of D near the
The map does not show capacity, opening hours, or how often or
4 cm × 500 m = 2,000 m = 2 km from A to B.
E.g. B is east of A; D is north of A and C north of B; square
ABCD is 2 km × 2 km = 4 km²; B is 40 m higher than A.
Reject the claim: a road symbol shows a connection, not how often
